deep.reconstruction:
Setting: the 1983-84 notes on arrangements (systèmes) of pseudo-lines. Grothendieck has built a cell complex X~, a kind of 'moduli complex' of arrangement types. The next page makes the dictionary explicit:
- faces = stable (simple, generic) configurations;
- edges = semi-stable configurations (one codimension-1 degeneration, e.g. a triangle collapsing to a triple point);
- vertices = critical configurations (codimension 2, here a 'critical' pseudo-line D passing through degenerate crossings).

He then treats X~ as a map in the sense of his cartographic formalism (Esquisse d'un programme). He works with the set of flags or 'regions' (vertex ⊂ edge ⊂ face, i.e. barycentric triangles), written X~^{dr?}, and the involutions σ0, σ1, σ2 on it:
- σ2 changes the face, fixing the incident edge (dim 1) and vertex (dim 0), as the page says;
- σ0 changes the vertex;
- σ1 changes the edge.

He first asks whether σ0 is the 'inverse' of σ2. He rejects this and introduces a fourth involution σ: the central symmetry of a region with respect to the vertex. This is meaningful because at a critical vertex the local picture of X~ is that of two crossing lines (the orange X's), so there is a well-defined opposite sector. σ commutes with σ2.

He arranges the four involutions in a chain σ1 – σ – σ2 – σ0 in which consecutive ones commute. So the group acting on flags is presented by involutions with commutation relations along a path, extending the cartographic group <σ0, σ1, σ2 | σi², (σ0σ2)²>.

He proposes to interpret the operations as acting on 'faisceaux' (local pencils of pseudo-lines). The opening lines say a flag/repère (D, s, ω, orientation) amounts to:
- a pencil associated to the vertex;
- together with a pinning (épinglage) of that pencil relative to the bigons it defines.

For σ1, orbits in X~^{dr}/σ1 correspond to singular vertices of X~. These are described by a stable configuration at the vertex plus two 'consecutive' triangles, giving rise to two sub-stable (semi-stable) configurations. Orientation data ω_a, ω_b, a, b are attached to the two crossing points of the critical line D. The other orientation data are induced by an orientation of the green bigon, the bigon swept when D is pushed off to either side, as shown in the middle drawing.

Orbits of the group generated by σ1 and σ (the transcription reads σ3, σ) are described by data of the neighbouring lines D_{1/2}, D_{2/3}, D_{5/6}, D_{6/7}, i.e. pseudo-lines inserted between consecutive members of the pencils.

The bottom drawing shows a critical pseudo-line D passing through two crossings ('arête de D', 'p.r. critique D'). The marginal note records a duality-type dictionary: faces ↔ faces, vertices ↔ lines, edges ↔ bijections of local angles.

Overall purpose: give a combinatorial-cartographic description of the complex of arrangement types (flip complex), via the action of a cartographic-type group on its flags, with local data read off from pencils, bigons and orientations.
errors: The stated relations are internally plausible: σ0 and σ2 commute as in the cartographic group, and the central symmetry σ commutes with σ2. However, the claim that σ1 commutes with σ is asserted, not verified on the page.

The interpretation of the X~^{..}/σ1 orbits as 'singular vertices' sits uneasily with σ1 being the edge-changing involution. Either the labelling of the σ's differs from the Esquisse convention, or the sentence is elliptic. This cannot be decided from this page.
The text reads '(σ3, σ)' where context suggests (σ1, σ). Either a fifth operation is meant or this is a slip/misreading.

ideas.what: Cell complex whose faces/edges/vertices are stable / semi-stable / critical pseudo-line configurations (the flip complex of arrangements with codimension-2 relations)
ideas.modern_name: Flip graph/complex of simple pseudoline arrangements; second higher Bruhat order B(n,2) and its 2-cells

ideas.what: Applying cartographic-group involutions σ0, σ1, σ2 to the flags of this complex, extended by a fourth involution σ (central symmetry at a critical vertex) in a chain σ1–σ–σ2–σ0 with consecutive commuting
ideas.modern_name: Cartographic group / flag (monodromy) group of a map, extended by a local antipodal involution
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck (Esquisse, 1984) for cartographic groups; Jones–Singerman for maps
ideas.where_published: Cartographic group σ0, σ1, σ2 in Esquisse d'un programme; its application to pseudo-line complexes is not published

ideas.what: Flags of the complex described as pencils of pseudo-lines with a pinning relative to the bigons they define, plus orientation data
ideas.modern_name: Local (oriented-matroid-type) data at codimension-2 strata; 'pinnings' in the sense of épinglages

ideas.what: Marginal dictionary faces↔faces, vertices↔lines, edges↔bijections of local angles
ideas.modern_name: Duality between arrangement and its dual/zonotopal tiling (rhombic tilings)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Folklore (duality pseudoline arrangements ↔ rhombic tilings of zonogons)

missed.claim: Grothendieck treats the moduli-type complex of pseudo-line arrangements (stable/semi-stable/critical strata) as a 'map' in his cartographic sense. He equips its flags with an extended involution group, linking dessins/cartographic groups to the combinatorics later formalized as higher Bruhat orders and flip complexes.
missed.quote: Sur X~, il y a les opérations σ1, σ, σ2, σ0 dont deux [consécutifs] commutant
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: The flip complex of pseudoline arrangements is studied via higher Bruhat orders and zonotopal tilings. A presentation of its flag group in cartographic terms, with an extra antipodal involution, is not standard. It suggests viewing these combinatorial moduli spaces through Grothendieck–Teichmüller-style 'tower' formalism.

missed.claim: Description of the orbits of the subgroups <σ1> and <σ1, σ> in terms of local data (pencils, bigons, inserted lines D_{i/i+1}) is begun but not completed.
missed.quote: les points de X~/(σ3,σ), qui sont formés de données de {D1/2, D2/3, D5/6, D6/7
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: A complete local classification would give an explicit combinatorial presentation of the codimension-2 structure of the arrangement complex. That is a minor but concrete open bookkeeping task.

deep.surprise_reason: Using the Esquisse cartographic formalism, with an added fourth involution, on the cell complex of pseudo-line arrangement types is an unpublished and somewhat original angle, contemporaneous with the Esquisse. The underlying combinatorics (flip complex, Ringel moves) is known, however, and the page is fragmentary.
transcription_corrections: The superscript on X~ (transcribed 'ex') may be 'dr' (drapeaux = flags), consistent with quotienting the flag set by σ1. This is uncertain.
The 'p.r.' / 'p.v.' abbreviation for stable/critical configurations recurs; its expansion (e.g. 'position relative') is uncertain, and the two transcriptions likely denote the same term.
'σ − σ2 − σ0 / σ1' is a small diagram (chain σ1–σ–σ2–σ0) rather than a subtraction.
Marginal note: 'faces ↔ faces / sommets ↔ droites / arêtes ↔ (bijections angles locaux)'.
'sommets singuliers' may read 'sommets ou arêtes singuliers'.
